title: Vennir API product (apis/<name>/api.yaml, kind: Api), format v2
description: A backend the team already runs, published through the install's gateway. Its OpenAPI file is the allowlist: the gateway forwards only requests whose method and path it describes, with only the query parameters it declares, and whose parameters, declared headers and body fit its schemas (a body only where it declares one, with a Content-Type it can check), and blocks everything else.

apiVersion.description: The catalog format: vennir.dev/v2. A file without it is from before v2: ./vennir catalog migrate rewrites it.

name.description: Its folder's name, apis/<name>/: callers reach it at /<team>/<name>/ on the gateway.

spec.description: Its OpenAPI file (3.0 or 3.1, YAML or JSON), beside api.yaml. Every operation in it is what may reach the backend; nothing else does.

backend.description: Where the gateway forwards to, and how it signs in there. The URL's host must be one this install's admins allow, or the API is held, not published.

url.description: The backend's base URL, https (http only for a Service inside the cluster); the spec's servers must include it.

auth.description: The credential the gateway adds to each request, minted per request from the API's own ServiceAccount; nothing is stored. Left out: none (the backend checks Vennir-Caller, or nothing).

serviceAccountToken.description: A token for the API's own Kubernetes ServiceAccount, for this audience: for a backend in a cluster that checks Kubernetes tokens. Never the Kubernetes API's, nor one a cloud federates (sts.amazonaws.com, api://AzureADTokenExchange, a GKE Workload Identity pool or a GCP workload identity provider): the catalog tool, the console and the gateway refuse those.

googleIdToken.description: A Google ID token for the backend (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, IAP), minted per request through the API ServiceAccount's federation: as serviceAccount, for audience (default: backend.url).

awsSigV4.description: For an AWS backend that takes IAM (a Lambda function URL, API Gateway): the gateway assumes roleArn with the API ServiceAccount's token (AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity: the role trusts this cluster's OIDC issuer for that ServiceAccount) and signs each request with SigV4 for service in region.

service.description: The SigV4 service name: lambda for a function URL, execute-api for API Gateway.

serviceAccount.description: The Kubernetes ServiceAccount, in the team's namespace, the gateway mints this API's backend credentials for (the console creates it). It ends in -api: the gateway may mint tokens for those ServiceAccounts and no others. Left out: <name>-api.

shareWith.description: Deprecated: access's grants replace it, made per install in the console, and it goes in the next release (vennir catalog validate warns). The other teams whose members and bots may call it, or ["*"] for every team. Left out, only its own team.

access.description: Who else may call it: each install's grants, to single sign-on groups and to users (people and bots), each with its rate, which the API's team's maintainers add in the console. This says how a request for access is answered.

requests.description: open: granted at once, at the default limit; approval (the default): the team's maintainers grant or decline it; closed: none are taken (grants already made stay until revoked).

visibility.description: listed (the default): every team sees it, and those it isn't shared with can ask for access. hidden: only its own team sees it, so it can't have shareWith.

deprecated.description: Marks it deprecated, saying what to use instead. It keeps working; the console shows the message to everyone who uses it.

reachable.description: cluster (the default): the gateway answers for it inside the cluster only. internet: also on the gateway's public address, if this install lets the team publish there.

limits.description: Requests per minute or second: default for every caller (its own team, a grant without a rate of its own, and each person in a group a grant names), and any calling team by name (its own, or a shareWith team).

timeout.description: How long the gateway waits for the backend's answer to begin, 1s to 300s (default 30s).

maxRequest.description: The largest request body it forwards, up to 10MiB (default 1MiB).
